article.story: LUBBOCK, Texas -- — Cruz Davis scored 20 points and No. 9 Texas Tech beat LSU New Orleans 86-41 on Wednesday night, extending its non-conference home winning streak to 51 games. Damarion Davis added 18 points for the Red Raiders (5-0), while Jamichael Stillwell had 11 points and 11 rebounds. Donovan Atwell also scored 11 as Texas Tech wrapped up a five-game homestand to begin the season. The Red Raiders scored the first 10 points and led 46-13 at halftime, when New Orleans had more turnovers (17) than points. Tech scored 24 points off those turnovers. Texas Tech has won 105 of its last 106 non-conference home games since 2013, with the lone loss coming 76-74 in overtime to No. 15 Kentucky on Jan. 25, 2020. That ended a school-record 54-game streak. Tech is 28-0 in such games under fourth-year coach Grant McCasland. Baylor has the nation’s longest current non-conference home winning streak at 56 games after beating Jackson State 104-55 earlier Wednesday. Auburn's 69-game streak ended with an 80-69 loss last Friday to No. 12 Arizona, a Big 12 team like Baylor and Texas Tech. Kedrick Osby had 12 points for New Orleans (2-2). The Red Raiders last week won 84-78 over then-No. 3 Illinois, the highest-ranked non-conference opponent they have beaten at home. The Fighting Illini won 99-78 at No. 5 Duke on Tuesday night, ending the Blue Devils’ 35-game home winning streak. Texas Tech, still without JT Toppin while the All-America forward recovers from a knee injury last February, won its other four games by an average of 37 points. Up next LSU New Orleans plays at Texas Southern on Saturday. Texas Tech plays No. 23 Louisville on Tuesday in the Players Era 16 tournament in Las Vegas. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
